conviction_note: Baseline median reaction is 5.9% with 4 of 7 prints up; I take a moderate negative because insiders filed three Rule 144 notices and two Form 4s inside one week in the middle of a +30% twenty-session melt-up, and the print arrives with the stock 5.5% from its 52-week high on 66m shares a day into a retail stream that is uniformly positioned for a squeeze - the bar has moved to an agentic-AI ARR acceleration that nothing in the capture evidences.

findings.finding: Insiders sold into the melt-up: Form 144 notices on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-19 with Form 4s on 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-19 - three intents-to-sell inside seven days - during exactly the run that took the stock 30.1% higher over twenty sessions to within 5.5% of its 52-week high, and there is no offsetting purchase anywhere in the index.
findings.corpus_ref: filings.json, Form 144 entries dated 2026-08-19, 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-13 and Form 4 entries dated 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-14
findings.why_not_priced: Form 144s are not indexed by any consumer aggregator, and the retail stream captured on the morning of the print - dozens of messages - never mentions insider selling once; it discusses only the short interest and how far the stock goes after hours. If the market had priced insiders exiting into the rally, the run-in would not be +30% and the stream would not read 'SNOW 2.0 today AH'.
findings.independence: The 30.1% twenty-session run-up and the 66.2m-share average daily volume come from the baseline tape rather than from any captured document, which makes the positioning half of this finding independently verifiable - but no second corpus document points the same way, so treat the insider half as single-sourced.

findings.finding: The print is arriving with the bar reset upward on the day itself: Needham raised its price target to $22.00 on the morning of 2026-09-03, the Estimize crowd sits $0.03 above Wall Street on EPS and $8.48m above on revenue, and a corpus item states 'institutional desks are monitoring this print with high intent to see if their new Agentic AI layer can drive a massive ARR beat' - so the requirement is an ARR acceleration, not a beat.
findings.corpus_ref: docs/94ca8769ddaff2dce7685a3314d1bc4d7ac00ae3.txt (snapshots/20260903T150821Z equivalent, captured 15:08Z on the event date and therefore pre-print for an after-the-close release), entries dated 2026-09-03T14:26:58Z, 2026-09-03T14:26:28Z and 2026-09-03T15:01:20Z
findings.why_not_priced: This is mostly priced, and I include it signed negative for one reason: a target raise on the morning of the print and a crowd consensus above the sell-side are both symptoms of expectation stacking, and the same corpus records short interest at 26% - which means a merely good print gets sold by the longs before the shorts are forced to cover. It is the weaker half of my case, hence the wide band crossing zero.
findings.independence: The 26% short-interest figure comes from a different corpus participant on the same morning and cuts the other way, which is why I am not larger than -3 overall: docs/94ca8769ddaff2dce7685a3314d1bc4d7ac00ae3.txt entry dated 2026-09-03T13:30:55Z

baseline_tension: It cuts hard against the run-up (+30.1% over twenty sessions, +94% off the 52-week low) and against the base rate (4 of 7 up, including +24.4% and +5.9% at the equivalent September print a year earlier), so this is an explicitly contrarian read on momentum.
corpus_limits: No option chain, so no implied move or skew, and no way to test whether a 26% short base is genuinely crowded. No news search was run for this ticker, so no consensus of record and no independent view of the agentic-AI ARR thesis; both of my findings rest on the EDGAR index and one Stocktwits body. This is an amc print, so the 2026-09-03 15:08Z sweep and price bar are pre-event and admissible; no item in this capture carried a non-empty tripwire_tells.
